'''Jacob''' ('''Yaqub''') '''H. Hanna''' ([[Arabic]]: '''Yaqub''' or '''Yaoub'''; born 26 August 1979)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Yakoub Hanna |url=https://www.myheritage.com/research/record-10826-4382482/yakoub-hanna-in-famous-people-throughout-history?tr_id=m_aut17ygxva_5qepr4tez6 |access-date=2023-08-24 |website=myheritage.com}}</ref> is a Palestinian biologist,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Gewin |first=Virginia |date=2010 |title=Turning point: Jacob Hanna |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=468 |issue=7321 |page=337 |doi=10.1038/nj7321-337a |issn=0028-0836|doi-access=free }}</ref> born with Israeli citizenship, who is working as a Full Professor in the Department of [[Molecular genetics|Molecular Genetics]] at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in [[Rehovot]], [[Israel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siegel-Itzkovich |first=Judy |date=2022-08-02 |title=Israeli scientists make model synthetic mouse embryo with stem cells |url=https://www.jpost.com/science/article-713690 |access-date=2023-08-24 |website=The Jerusalem Post |language=en-US}}</ref> An expert in embryonic [[stem cell research]], he is most recognized for developing the first ''bona fide'' '''S'''tructured '''S'''tem cell-derived '''S'''ynthetic '''E'''mbryo '''M'''odels ('''SEM'''s) in the [[petri dish]] in mice and humans.<ref Hanna pioneered the extended static and dynamic post-implantation ex utero whole embryo growth platform<ref name=":6" /> that was critical for enabling the synthetic and structured  embryo model establishment,<ref name=":12" /> and also pioneered developing the technology to generate alternative naive-like and naive pluripotent states in humans, that correspond to more early stages in development and retain an enhanced potential to make essential extra-embryonic tissue (e.g. placenta and yolk-sac),<ref name=":17" /><ref name=":16" /> which proved essential for generating the first complete synthetic embryo models by his team<ref name=":13">{{cite journal |last1=Oldak |first1=Bernardo |last2=Wildschutz |first2=Emilie |biorxiv=10.1101/2023.06.14.544922 |language=en |last3=Bondarenko |first3=Vladyslav |last4=Aguilera-Castrejon |first4=Alejandro |last5=Zhao |first5=Cheng |last6=Tarazi |first6=Shadi |last7=Comar |first7=Mehmet-Yunus |last8=Ashouokhi |first8=Shahd |last9=Lokshtanov |first9=Dmitry |title=Complete human day 14 post-implantation embryo models from naive ES cells |journal=Nature |date=2023 |volume=622 |issue=7983 |pages=562–573 |doi=10.1038/s41586-023-06604-5 |pmid=37673118 |pmc=10584686 |bibcode=2023Natur.622..562O }}</ref><ref name=":23" /><ref name=":12" /> and solely from such naive pluripotent cells.

== Education ==
Hanna has a PhD in microbiology and immunology and an MD in clinical medicine from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=האקדמיה הלאומית הישראלית למדעים The Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities - Jacob Hanna |url=https://academy.ac.il/RichText/GeneralPage.aspx?nodeId=1436 |access-date=2023-08-24 |website=The Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities |language=en}}</ref> To train in stem cell research, he worked from 2007 to 2011 as a Helen Hay Whitney - Novartis postdoctoral fellow and a Genzyme postdoctoral fellow at the [[Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research]] at MIT,<ref name=":26">{{Cite journal |last1=Hanna |first1=Jacob |last2=Saha |first2=Krishanu |last3=Pando |first3=Bernardo |last4=van Zon |first4=Jeroen |last5=Lengner |first5=Christopher J. |last6=Creyghton |first6=Menno P. |last7=van Oudenaarden |first7=Alexander |last8=Jaenisch |first8=Rudolf |date=December 2009 |title=Direct cell reprogramming is a stochastic process amenable to acceleration |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=462 |issue=7273 |pages=595–601 |bibcode=2009Natur.462..595H |doi=10.1038/nature08592 |issn=1476-4687 |pmc=2789972 |pmid=19898493 |hdl=1721.1/58480}}</ref> Cambridge, Massachusetts, under [[Rudolf Jaenisch]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2011, Hanna joined the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] as an assistant professor in 2011, and has been there ever since. In 2018, Hanna received academic tenure and promotion at the Department of Molecular Genetics in the Weizmann Institute, and in 2023 became a Full Professor of Stem Cell Biology and Synthetic Embryology.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |title=Jacob H Hanna |url=https://app.dimensions.ai/details/entities/publication/author/ur.0643150035.03 |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=Dimensions.ai}}</ref><ref name="weizmann.ac.il">{{Cite web |title=Jacob (Yaqub) Hanna {{!}} Department of Molecular Genetics |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/molgen/jacob-yaqub-hanna-0 |access-date=2023-09-09 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il}}</ref>

Hanna was listed in 2014 among top 40 under 40 leading international scientists by Cell journal<ref name="Guidance" /> and elected to the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 2018.<ref name=":32" /> In 2021, he was announced as the top thinker of the year 2021 by [[Prospect (magazine)|''Prospect'']] magazine for his works on embryology.<ref name=":33" /> His extended ex utero embryo culture was selected among Science Magazine Breakthrough of the year 2021,<ref name=":38" /> and his mouse complete synthetic embryo models were selected by Nature magazine among seven technologies to watch in 2023.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-023-00178-y | doi=10.1038/d41586-023-00178-y | title=Seven technologies to watch in 2023 | date=2023 | last1=Eisenstein | first1=Michael | journal=Nature | volume=613 | issue=7945 | pages=794–797 | pmid=36690758 | bibcode=2023Natur.613..794E | url-access=subscription }}</ref> Human complete stem-cell derived embryo model generated by Hanna was selected by [[Time (magazine)|TIME]] in its featured list of inventions in 2023,<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://time.com/collection/best-inventions-2023/6324143/human-embryo-model/#:~:text=Hanna%27s%20team%20used%20naive%20stem,to%20grow%20for%2014%20days | title=Human Embryo Model: The 200 Best Inventions of 2023 | magazine=Time | date=24 October 2023 }}</ref> and the generation of synthetic embryo models of development through using stem cells was selected as the method of the year 2023 by Nature Methods.<ref name=":39">{{Cite journal |date=December 2023 |title=Method of the Year 2023: methods for modeling development |journal=Nature Methods |language=en |volume=20 |issue=12 |pages=1831–1832 |doi=10.1038/s41592-023-02134-0 |pmid=38057526 |issn=1548-7105|doi-access=free }}</ref>  He is the recipient of the 2025 Nakasone Award by the Human Frontiers Science Program – HFSP for ''"'' developing synthetic embryo models from naïve pluripotent stem cells, which provides a new foundation for developmental biology and regenerative medicine strategies."[https://www.hfsp.org/hfsp-nakasone-award/2025-jacob-yaqub-hanna][https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6y8D5YcBllY&t=4s&ab_channel=HFSP (Hanna's 2025 Nakasone Award Lecture])

== Early life ==
Hanna was born in [[Rameh]], an [[Arab citizens of Israel|Arab]] [[Local council (Israel)|village]] in the [[Galilee|Galilee region]] of [[Israel]] to a Palestinian Christian family.<ref name=":1" /> His father was a pediatrician and his mother was a high-school biology teacher. His grandfather was also a doctor in this village.<ref name="icrfonline">{{cite web |last1=Luxner |first1=Larry |title=Curing infertility after chemotherapy: This Israeli-Arab scientist may have the key |url=https://www.icrfonline.org/news/curing-infertility-after-chemotherapy-this-israeli-arab-scientist-may-have-the-key/ |publisher=Israel Cancer Research Fund |access-date=12 September 2024}}</ref> He studied medical science at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, obtaining a B.Sc. degree ''[[summa cum laude]]'' in 2001, and then continued to do an M.D.-Ph.D. degree at the same institute. He indicated in his interviews that his decision to undertake a career in research was heavily influenced and inspired by the success of his uncle, Nabil Hanna, who invented the first [[FDA]]-approved antibody therapy in humans ([[Rituximab|Rituxan]], a blockbuster anti-CD20 mAb drug for treatment of [[non-Hodgkin lymphoma]]) while serving as chief scientific office of [[IDEC Pharmaceuticals]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-06-25 |title=A winning pair {{!}} Two Weizmann scientists chosen by Cell magazine {{!}} WeizmannCompass |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/WeizmannCompass/sections/briefs/a-winning-pair |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref> His Ph.D. research was supervised by {{ill|Ofer Mandelboim|he|עופר מנדלבוים}} and was on the roles of [[natural killer cells]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hanna |first1=Jacob |last2=Mandelboim |first2=Ofer |date=2007 |title=When killers become helpers |journal=Trends in Immunology |volume=28 |issue=5 |pages=201–206 |doi=10.1016/j.it.2007.03.005 |issn=1471-4906 |pmid=17403615}}</ref> In 2007, the Hebrew University awarded him both Ph.D. in microbiology and immunology and M.D. in clinical medicine ''[[summa cum laude]]''.<ref name=":2" /> Hanna's three sisters also studied medicine in the Hebrew University.<ref name="icrfonline"/>

Hanna decided not to go into practicing medicine but focus only on developing his research career in Academia. In 2007, he received the [[Helen Hay Whitney Foundation]], and later a [[Genzyme]]-Whitehead Fellowship for outstanding postdoctoral fellows in 2009, by which he worked at the [[Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research]] in Cambridge, Massachusetts.<ref name=":0" /> His research there till early 2011 under [[Rudolf Jaenisch]] helped him specialize in [[pluripotent stem cell]] research and [[induced pluripotent stem cell]] reprogramming.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and discoveries ==

=== Induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming ===
During his postdoctoral research at the Whitehead Institute, Hanna focused on studying [[embryonic stem cells]] (ESCs) and [[epigenetic]] reprogramming of somatic cells into ESC-like cells, called induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). He developed [[transgenic mouse]] models to address problems in stem cell research. In 2007, he provided the first evidence that iPSCs could be used for a blood genetic disease, [[sickle cell anemia]], by combined [[Gene therapy|gene]] and [[cell therapy]] approach in mice.<ref name="Hanna 1920–1923">{{Cite journal |last1=Hanna |first1=Jacob |last2=Wernig |first2=Marius |last3=Markoulaki |first3=Styliani |last4=Sun |first4=Chiao-Wang |last5=Meissner |first5=Alexander |last6=Cassady |first6=John P. |last7=Beard |first7=Caroline |last8=Brambrink |first8=Tobias |last9=Wu |first9=Li-Chen |last10=Townes |first10=Tim M. |last11=Jaenisch |first11=Rudolf |date=2007-12-21 |title=Treatment of Sickle Cell Anemia Mouse Model with iPS Cells Generated from Autologous Skin |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1152092 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=318 |issue=5858 |pages=1920–1923 |doi=10.1126/science.1152092 |issn=0036-8075 |pmid=18063756 |bibcode=2007Sci...318.1920H |s2cid=657569|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His supervisor, Jaenisch was awarded the Masri Prize and the Wolf Prize in 2011 for this research innovation, as the award citation read: "For demonstration that iPS cells can be used to cure genetic disease in a mammal, thus establishing their therapeutic potential".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-12-11 |title=Rudolf Jaenisch |url=https://wolffund.org.il/2018/12/11/rudolf-jaenisch/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200112211407/https://wolffund.org.il/2018/12/11/rudolf-jaenisch/ |archive-date=January 12, 2020 |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US }}</ref>

Hanna made scientific contributions to understanding the iPSC phenomenon in its early days. He developed a novel inducible "reprogrammable mouse" transgenic models with drug controlled over expression of the [[Shinya Yamanaka|Yamanaka]] reprogramming factors'''.''' This technique allowed him to create reprogrammed [[B lymphocytes]] carrying endogenous genetic rearrangements of the [[B-cell receptor]] (BCR) into iPSCs, thus providing definitive proof for the feasibility of reprogramming terminally differentiated cells to iPSCs that carried the original genetic rearrangement mark of the BCR.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hanna |first1=Jacob |last2=Markoulaki |first2=Styliani |last3=Schorderet |first3=Patrick |last4=Carey |first4=Bryce W. |last5=Beard |first5=Caroline |last6=Wernig |first6=Marius |last7=Creyghton |first7=Menno P. |last8=Steine |first8=Eveline J. |last9=Cassady |first9=John P. |last10=Foreman |first10=Ruth |last11=Lengner |first11=Christopher J. |last12=Dausman |first12=Jessica A. |last13=Jaenisch |first13=Rudolf |date=April 2008 |title=Direct Reprogramming of Terminally Differentiated Mature B Lymphocytes to Pluripotency |url=|journal=Cell |volume=133 |issue=2 |pages=250–264 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2008.03.028 |issn=0092-8674 |pmc=2615249 |pmid=18423197}}</ref>

From 2013, Hanna worked as the Robertson Stem Cell Investigator of The New York Stem Cell Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacob Hanna, MD, PhD |url=https://nyscf.org/people/jacob-hanna-md-phd/ |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=New York Stem Cell Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> His first major achievement under the NYSCF research was the demonstration that human naïve-like ES/iPS cell state tin NHSM naive-like conditions that he discovered (and later also in HENSM naive conditions), has additional unique functional properties compared to conventional primed iPS cells, which is the creation of sperm and egg stem cells from human skin cell derived naive-like iPSCs,<ref>{{Cite web |title=In a First, Weizmann Institute and Cambridge University Scientists Create Human Primordial Germ Cells |url=https://www.newswise.com/articles/in-a-first-weizmann-institute-and-cambridge-university-scientists-create-human-primordial-germ-cells |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=www.newswise.com |language=en}}</ref> which has not been possible thus far with conventional human iPSCs. The experiment, done in collaboration with [[Azim Surani]]'s team at the [[University of Cambridge]], was published in the journal ''[[Cell (journal)|Cell]]'' in 2015.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Irie |first1=Naoko |last2=Weinberger |first2=Leehee |last3=Tang |first3=Walfred W. He also said "I think it's good, I thinks it's done very well, it's all making sense and I'm pretty impressed with it".<ref name=":25" />

==== Synthetic stem-cell-derived embryo model research related ethical discussions ====
In 2022, when Hanna published the first bona fide mouse synthetic embryo with definitive proof of completing the process of germ-layer gastrulation and early organogenesis formation of beating heart and brain folds, he reported to the ''[[MIT Technology Review]]'' that he was already using the same method to make human embryo models (which indeed he was the first to report in 2023).<ref name=":13" /><ref name=":23" /><ref name=":20" /> The funder company, NFX, stated that the aim is "renewing human health—making all of us young and healthy."<ref name=":272">{{Cite web |last=Regalado |first=Antonio |date=2022-08-04 |title=This startup wants to copy you into an embryo for organ harvesting |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/in-breakthrough-israeli-scientists-say-they-synthesized-human-embryos-from-stem-cells/ |access-date=2023-09-01 |website=Times of Israel |language=en-US}}</ref> and "groundbreaking advance" in science.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Devlin |first=Hannah |date=2023-06-14 |title=Synthetic human embryos created in groundbreaking advance that are followed in most countries.<ref name=":29">{{Cite journal |last1=Lovell-Badge |first1=Robin |last2=Anthony |first2=Eric |last3=Barker |first3=Roger A. |last4=Bubela |first4=Tania |last5=Brivanlou |first5=Ali H. |last6=Carpenter |first6=Melissa |last7=Charo |first7=R. Alta |last8=Clark |first8=Amander |last9=Clayton |first9=Ellen |last10=Cong |first10=Yali |last11=Daley |first11=George Q. |last12=Fu |first12=Jianping |last13=Fujita |first13=Misao |last14=Greenfield |first14=Andy |last15=Goldman |first15=Steve A. |display-authors=8 |date=2021-06-08 |title=ISSCR Guidelines for Stem Cell Research and Clinical Translation: The 2021 update |journal=Stem Cell Reports |volume=16 |issue=6 |pages=1398–1408 |doi=10.1016/j.stemcr.2021.05.012 |issn=2213-6711 |pmc=8190668 |pmid=34048692}}</ref> However, the guidelines or any other legislations do not cover stem cell-derived embryo models,<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=Ball |first=Philip |date=2023-06-13 |title='Embryo Models' Challenge Legal, Ethical and Biological Concepts |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/embryo-models-challenge-legal-ethical-and-biological-concepts-20230613/ |website=Quanta Magazine}}</ref> as the embryo models are made from ordinary cells.<ref name=":262" /> Hanna commented on [[Stat (website)|Stat]]: "You don't ban nuclear physics because somebody can make a nuclear bomb."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wosen |first=Jonathan |date=2023-02-13 |title='It is a balance': Scientists grapple with ethics of cutting-edge stem cell research |url=https://www.statnews.com/2023/02/13/scientists-grapple-with-ethics-of-cutting-edge-stem-cell-research/ |access-date=2023-09-02 |website=STAT |language=en-US}}</ref>

Rivron, Martinez Arias and others, writing on the ethical issues in ''Cell'' in 2023, expressed a possible need to open discussions about revising the definition of an embryo since certain embryo models can theoretically become functional embryos and produce babies.<ref name=":22" /><ref name=":24">{{Cite journal |last1=Rivron |first1=Nicolas C. |last2=Martinez Arias |first2=Alfonso |last3=Pera |first3=Martin F. |last4=Moris |first4=Naomi |last5=M'hamdi |first5=Hafez Ismaili |date=2023-08-17 |title=An ethical framework for human embryology with embryo models |journal=Cell |volume=186 |issue=17 |pages=3548–3557 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2023.07.028 |issn=1097-4172 |pmid=37595564 |s2cid=260960847 |doi-access=free |hdl-access=free |hdl=10230/58014}}</ref> [[Robin Lovell-Badge]], at the Francis Crick Institute and member of the ISSCR guidelines preparation, also agreed that both natural and synthetic human embryo models should be regulated equally, saying, "These models do challenge the need to stick to the 14-day rule", referring the ISSCR's relaxation in 2021 the limit of growing human embryos up to 14 days.<ref name=":29" /><ref name=":27" /> The scientific and ethical complexity were remarked by J. Benjamin Hurlbut, bioethicist at the Arizona State University: "The big question is how the boundary between a tissue culture and a human organism is going to be drawn and on what criteria."<ref name=":262" /> Pompeu Fabra University Professor Alfonso Martinez Arias, Ph.D., whose own lab is working on building human embryo models, noted that such conversations and debates are nothing new and should be welcomed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helen |first=Floresh |date=Sep 8, 2023 |title=Human embryo models offer window into early development |url=https://www.fiercebiotech.com/research/new-human-embryo-models-offer-window-earliest-stages-development}}</ref> The [[International Society for Stem Cell Research]] publicly announced support for the research<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-26 |title=The ISSCR Statement on New Research with Embryo Models |url=https://www.isscr.org/isscr-news/isscr-statement-on-new-research-with-embryo-models |access-date=2023-09-02 |website=International Society for Stem Cell Research |language=en-US}}</ref> and highlighted to the public that such complete embryo models are only models of embryogenesis and should not be considered as embryos. British science writer, [[Philip Ball]], alleviated concern related to this line of research by emphasizing that "None [of the embryo models] has the potential to grow into a human being, nor is there any reason why scientists would want them to."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ball |first=Philip |date=2023-07-01 |title=Are human embryo models a cause for hope or alarm? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2023/jul/01/are-human-embryo-models-a-cause-for-hope-or-alarm |access-date=2023-09-01 |work=The Observer |language=en-GB |issn=0029-7712}}</ref> Upon publication of Hanna's ground breaking paper on human complete stem cell-derived embryo models (termed SEMs) in Nature in 2023,<ref name=":23" /> [[Philip Ball]] tweeted, "This is work at the absolute forefront of this extraordinary and exciting field".<ref>{{Cite web |title=@philipcball |url=https://twitter.com/philipcball/status/1699514411948384573?s=20 |access-date=2023-09-08 |website=X (formerly Twitter) |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Hanna openly identifies as non-binary.<ref name=":33" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Obedin-Maliver |first1=Juno |last2=Ochu |first2=Erinma |last3=Zhong |first3=Franklin |last4=Shaikh |first4=Aqsa |last5=Hanna |first5=Jacob H. |last6=Foley |first6=Edan |date=August 2022 |title=Pride in STEM worldwide |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0092867422009801 |journal=Cell |language=en |volume=185 |issue=17 |pages=3070–3072 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2022.07.027 |pmid=35985282 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1432780949318782989 |user=jacob_hanna |title=I find it quite funny that I was ranked #1 on the list of 50 thinkers by Prospect Magazine for 2021. Thanks to everyone for their support and @prospect_uk for covering our field. |first=Jacob |last=Hanna |date=August 31, 2021}}</ref> He was born as a Protestant, although he states that his family is not particularly religious.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ansede |first=Manuel |date=June 14, 2024 |title=Jacob Hanna, biologist: 'If a human fetus model is controversial, I will make it without a heart or brain' |url=https://english.elpais.com/science-tech/2024-06-14/jacob-hanna-biologist-if-a-human-fetus-model-is-controversial-i-will-make-it-without-a-heart-or-brain.html |website=[[El País]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=St. Fleur |first=Nicholas |date=March 4, 2024 |title=Q&A: Stem cell biologist predicts human embryo models could pave the way to organ transplants |url=https://www.statnews.com/2024/03/04/jacob-hanna-human-embryo-models-organ-transplants/ |website=[[Stat (website)|STAT News]]}}</ref>

* The Nakasone Award by the Human Frontiers Science Program – HFSP (2025) [https://www.hfsp.org/hfsp-nakasone-award/2025-jacob-yaqub-hanna][https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6y8D5YcBllY&t=4s&ab_channel=HFSP Hanna's Nakasone Award Lecture]
* ISF Breakthrough Award (Israeli Science Foundation equivalent to NIH Director's Pioneer Award)[https://www.isf.org.il/Files/Announcement/%D7%A8%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%AA%20%D7%96%D7%95%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%9D%202025.pdf]
* Named on the 2024 STATUS List by STAT news, a prestigious list with most influential individuals in healthcare, medicine, & life sciences [https://www.statnews.com/status-list/2024/jacob-hanna/][https://www.statnews.com/status-list/2024/]
* Human complete synthetic embryo model generated by Hanna was selected by the Time as invention breakthrough of the year 2023 [https://time.com/collection/best-inventions-2023/6324143/human-embryo-model/#:~:text=Hanna's%20team%20used%20naive%20stem,to%20grow%20for%2014%20days.],
* The generation of synthetic embryo models was selected as the method of the year 2023 by Nature Methods journal on behalf of Nature publishing group.<ref name=":39" />
* Mouse and human complete synthetic embryo models were selected by Nature magazine among seven technologies to watch in [https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-023-00178-y 2023]. 
* The IVI Foundation Award for Basic Research in Reproductive Medicine (2023)
* Manuscript describing mouse synthetic stem cell-derived embryo models among the 10 selected "Best of Cell 2022" publications by ''Cell'' journal editors (2023)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Best of Cell 2022 |url=https://info.cell.com/best-of-cell-2022 |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=info.cell.com |language=en}}</ref>
* The 2022 paper on stem cell-derived (synthetic) embryogenesis listed among top scientific breakthroughs of the year 2022 by ''[[The Atlantic]]'' magazine<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Derek |date=2022-12-08 |title=Breakthroughs of the Year |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/newsletters/archive/2022/12/technology-medicine-law-ai-10-breakthroughs-2022/672390/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=The Atlantic |language=en}}</ref> and ''[[The Week]]'' Magazine (2023)<ref>{{Cite web |title=18 recent scientific breakthroughs |url=https://theweek.com/health-and-science/1019386/recent-scientific-breakthroughs |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=The Week |language=en}}</ref>
